correctness.rationale: The assigned RESULT.md identifies selected fiber sections S_h, and uses the selected inter-fiber matching-edge graph T. Induced connectivity makes T connected. Any two consecutive T edges u-v-w force the unique base geodesic u-v-w (no triangles or four-cycles). If matching colors equal, the center (v,a) blocks their unique geodesic; if different, any one-color-change shortest product route meets selected (v,a) or (v,b). Thus at most two base fibers. For two adjacent fibers A,B, connectivity requires intersection; if intersection contains two colors, both length-two routes for a cross-colored pair are blocked; exactly one common color is also sufficient by two available shortest routes. Each non-common color has exactly three labelled choices: absent/in A/in B, yielding qz²(1+2z)^(q-1) per edge, disjoint from single fibers. Full maximum, maximality and singleton extension follow. Explicitly computed original-independent BFS connectivity, shortest path visibility and 2^6/2^9 subsets for H=K2/P3,q=3: cardinality profiles (6,9,14,12) and (9,15,27,24). Finite tests support but do not establish the universal girth result.
